textRun.content: Your personal guide to government benefits
A resident-first path from one plain-language story to trusted programs and guided applications.
Open with the 1:27 BenefitBeacon introduction video if time allows. Then say: “BenefitBeacon helps residents find the right starting point without knowing an agency or program name.”
Presentation goal: explain the access problem, demonstrate the resident journey, and show why the architecture is trustworthy and resilient.
The benefit access gap is measurable
NCOA estimates for older adults use 2023 participation data and published average benefit values.
Estimated annual gap across SNAP, SSI, and Medicare Savings Programs
Estimated annual gap across the same three programs
NCOA's estimated 2023 annual gap for older adults
County and state values are derived estimates using NCOA nonparticipant counts and benefit assumptions.

These figures estimate missed program benefits, not unclaimed property. NCOA and the Urban Institute estimate that eligible adults age 65 and older left $58 billion unclaimed in 2023 across SNAP, Supplemental Security Income, and Medicare Savings Programs.

Santa Clara County estimate: NCOA reports 39,962 eligible SNAP nonparticipants, 27,582 eligible SSI nonparticipants, and 22,687 eligible Medicare Savings Program nonparticipants. Applying NCOA's national monthly benefit assumptions of $188 for SNAP, $552.29 for SSI, and $164.90 for MSP produces an estimated annual gap of $317,846,461, shown as approximately $318 million.

California estimate: NCOA reports 855,248 eligible SNAP nonparticipants, 602,919 eligible SSI nonparticipants, and 537,779 eligible MSP nonparticipants. Applying the same assumptions produces $6,989,430,187, shown as approximately $7.0 billion.
These program counts may overlap because a person can qualify for more than one program. NCOA does not publish a Sunnyvale-only estimate, so the slide uses Santa Clara County as the local figure.
- NCOA, Benefits Participation Map and 2023 data export: https://www.ncoa.org/benefits-participation-map/

- NCOA, 9 Million Older Adults Missing Out on $58 Billion: https://www.ncoa.org/article/over-9-million-eligible-older-adults-are-missing-out-on-58-billion-in-benefits-that-can-help-them-afford-basic-necessities/

- NCOA and Urban Institute technical report: https://assets.ncoa.org/ffacfe7d-10b6-0083-2632-604077fd4eca/3462824a-d7e9-4ddb-a936-7c2172599005/Estimated_Program_Participation_Rates_for_Adults_65_and_Older_2023.pdf
Residents should not need to know the system
The burden today is on the person asking for help.
Programs are scattered across city, county, state, federal, utility, and community websites.
Eligibility language is hard to compare, and missing information can feel like a rejection.
The guidance often ends exactly when a resident reaches the official form.
The goal is not more information. It is a clear next action.

Use a resident example: “I am in Sunnyvale, my water bill is high, and I may need help fixing a leak.” Today that person must know which city, utility, county, state, or federal site to search. BenefitBeacon starts from the story instead.
One conversation creates a guided path
Questions are optional. The resident stays in control of what they share.
Use natural language or choose a sample prompt.
Answer or skip focused follow-up questions.
See relevant programs with published rules and sources.
Ask questions, then continue on the official site with the side-panel guide.

Walk through the four stages. Emphasize that every follow-up is optional and is asked only when it can materially improve the shortlist or answer. Residents can also browse all programs without sharing personal information.
Every result is built to be checked
AI explains the match. Published rules and program administrators decide.
Lower-income Sunnyvale homeowners who are seniors or have a disability
A short explanation based only on the facts the resident chose to share.
Ask about documents, next steps, deadlines, or published eligibility.

This is the trust moment. Each result preserves the curated program name, benefit, published eligibility text, official source, and freshness date. The AI may explain relevance, but it cannot rewrite these facts or claim final eligibility.
The generated SQL snapshot contains 62 records checked 2026-10-23; 52 records serve Sunnyvale.
The guide stays beside the official application
The resident does not lose context when they leave the discovery page.
Find a relevant program and understand why it may apply.
Ask source-grounded questions about eligibility and documents.
Explain visible fields and offer resident-approved safe fills.
No form submission, signature, sensitive identifier, consent, or verification bypass.

Demonstrate the handoff from a program result to the official application. The side panel carries only the selected program, a constrained profile, and bounded conversation context. It can explain fields and offer safe fills after the resident approves the site. It does not submit forms or fill sensitive identifiers.
A practical architecture built for reliability

High-level stack: React 19 and TypeScript with a Next.js-compatible App Router, Vinext/Vite, Cloudflare Worker-compatible APIs, D1/SQLite, deterministic 128-dimensional local embeddings, optional OpenAI Responses API calls, official web search for current program questions, and a Manifest V3 browser extension.
The critical reliability point: normal indexed discovery does not require live search, and deterministic ranking remains available when OpenAI times out.
Live demo: from a need to an application
“I live in Sunnyvale. My water bill is high, and I think I may have a leak.”
Enter the story in natural language
Skip or answer one optional question
Open a water-related program and ask what is needed
Launch the official site with BenefitBeacon beside it
3. Answer or skip a follow-up to show resident control.
4. Select a water or utility program.
5. Ask: “What documents should I have ready?”
6. Click Apply with BenefitBeacon and open the extension side panel.
If the network or AI service is unavailable, use Show all available programs and explain the deterministic fallback.
Find the help. Follow the path.

Close with: “Public benefits should not depend on knowing the right agency, acronym, or search terms. BenefitBeacon gives residents a trustworthy starting point and stays with them through the next step.”
Invite questions or return to the live product.
